evidence: I ran the skill's prescribed grep (quality-checks.md:26) case-insensitively, extended with gate|probe|polish|visual|functional|verifier|grader|oracle, over instruction.md and all three environment/instructions/*.md notes. It returned zero matches. I also grepped the brief, notes, seed_data.json and the agent Dockerfile for all 28 criterion ids (e.g. wall_every_route, sent_once_in_order, refusal_in_place), every JUDGE-* probe literal used in the judge.toml files (JUDGE-CS0..CS2, JUDGE-W0, JUDGE-WL0/1, JUDGE-ME1/2, JUDGE-H1C, JUDGE-R1B, JUDGE-D1, JUDGE-F1, JUDGE-O, JUDGE-TE, JUDGE-X0/1), the weights 0.6/0.2, floor, all_pass and likert. None of them appear. The agent Dockerfile copies only instructions/ and assets/, never tests/ or solution/ (environment/Dockerfile:14-15), so no test paths reach the agent. A word 8-gram overlap scan of brief+notes against every tests/**/*.md and *.toml file found a longest shared run of 9 tokens, in scored/functional/judge.toml: 'type @ in the message box the app suggests'. That is a restated public requirement (conversations.md:21), not grader vocabulary. The other overlap (8 tokens) is the demo-account table shared with tests/app_context.md, which the skill lists as intentional. The brief's only process language is a human request to try the app in a browser (instruction.md:9); it names no tool, judge or score. 'On hold' (conversations.md:13) is a product requirement, not a sentinel. Weak or alternative-app angle: this row concerns the agent-visible text only, so no app behaviour can change it. No grader literal is visible that would let a model pre-satisfy a probe or game a dimension.
